AccountMemory.description:
An account beside a client story card (3.B17, D25): its naming, current state and what happened after the card's call,
from WIA's records only. `internal_since` are internal meetings' remarks, for the reviewer only.
AccountMemory.title: AccountMemory

Alert.description: One failure alert (6.B4). `alert_id` is null for the scheduler's silence, which is read live and cannot be dismissed.
Alert.title: Alert

AlertList.description:
GET /alerts: the open alerts first; with ?resolved=true also those resolved in the last 14 days. Alert emails are
off (the owner, 25 October 2026): the app is the channel.
AlertList.title: AlertList

AngleBody.description: content_body of an angle: a strategist card (`card`), a strategic opportunity (`strategy`) or a legacy angle.
AngleBody.title: AngleBody

AngleDecision.description: Gate 1 for a card: a disposition (E.B20), or the earlier approve or reject for earlier angles.
AngleDecision.title: AngleDecision

Attestation.description: Who stated a fact at a gate, and when (R57). A paraphrase is a client's words in the approver's: never a quote.
Attestation.title: Attestation

BlockerItem.description: One thing that stops approval, in a reviewer's words (5.F2, R50).
BlockerItem.title: BlockerItem

BriefAnchor.description: The piece production writes first (E.B23, briefs/handoff.py): a person's choice at Gate 2, else the rule's.
BriefAnchor.title: BriefAnchor

BriefBodyV3.description: The writer's body with the ledger built after writing.

wia_perspective.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. WIA's belief or practice, as Whitney would say it
wia_perspective.title: Wia Perspective

BriefBodyV3.title: BriefBodyV3

central_point.description: The idea's point in one sentence: a WIA belief, standard or client experience, never a platform or tactic
central_point.title: Central Point

wia_perspective.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. WIA's belief or practice, as Whitney would say it
wia_perspective.title: Wia Perspective

BriefCTA.description: {choice, track, action, offer_connection, chosen_by} (R46). A writer may propose; only a person confirms.
BriefCTA.title: BriefCTA

BriefContentV3.description:
A version 3 brief (E.B23): the writer's copy with the claims ledger built after writing; `review.ledger` records
the ledger's verifier and `review.repair` whether a repair ran and was accepted.
BriefContentV3.title: BriefContentV3

BriefContentV4.description:
A version 4 brief (E.B33): the brief in the 13 October order and the finished copy of every asset (each Reel with its
kind, cover, on-screen hook and caption; the carousel's title and caption; the email's send header), with v3's ledger.
BriefContentV4.title: BriefContentV4

BriefEvidence.description: An EvidenceItem as a stored brief or research dossier carries it: the defaulted fields are all present.
BriefEvidence.title: BriefEvidence

BriefHandoff.description:
The version-independent production hand-off of a brief (E.B23, briefs/handoff.py). Production reads this, never the
contract-specific document, and acts only when `can_consume` is true.
BriefHandoff.title: BriefHandoff

BriefPublished.description: A published piece linked to a brief (L.B9): the captured final, its central point and the recorded edit.
BriefPublished.title: BriefPublished

BriefWriteResult.description:
What a brief write answers: a new version (edit, answers, review, clearance, CTA, refinement) or the decision. An
approval of a v4 brief with packs on also starts its content pack (`pack_run`).
BriefWriteResult.title: BriefWriteResult

body.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The finished caption after the hook, in paragraphs
body.title: Body

ending.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The caption's last line: its ask or closing thought, and any sign-off
ending.title: Ending

hook.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The caption's first line, distinct from the Reel's hook
hook.title: Hook

CardCheck.description: Where a card version's comparison check stands (E.B16, E.B20): a reframe, revive or edit queues one.
CardCheck.title: CardCheck

CardRefresh.description:
A refresh with feedback asked for on this card version (3.B7): queued, being written, waiting for this week's refreshes
budget, or failed; `message` says why it waits or failed, in plain words. A finished refresh is a new version carrying
its own `content_body.refresh`.
CardRefresh.title: CardRefresh

CardRefreshRecord.description:
Who made a refreshed card version (3.B7, R58): the model, from a reviewer's feedback; the fields it kept as a
person wrote them and the ones it changed.
CardRefreshRecord.title: CardRefreshRecord

CardRefreshRequest.description: Refresh with feedback (3.B7): a new card version written from the reviewer's words; fields a person edited stay.
CardRefreshRequest.title: CardRefreshRequest

job.description: Direction: a short note to the person who makes the asset; never published. What the carousel does for the reader
job.title: Job

caption.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The carousel's own caption; null only outside the caption channel

job.description: Direction: a short note to the person who makes the asset; never published. What the carousel does for the reader: it goes deeper than the Reels
job.title: Job

offer_descriptor.description: Where this asset names an offer: that offer's approved descriptor, word for word from the offer descriptors in the knowledge base; null when it names none
offer_descriptor.title: Offer Descriptor

register.description: written: slides and captions are clean and declarative
register.title: Register

title.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The carousel's title; slide 1 carries its promise
title.title: Title

ChunkSummary.description: A transcript chunk: the header names the call, date, type, client and speakers; `text` is the turns.
ChunkSummary.title: ChunkSummary

CostGroup.description: One group of recorded cost (6.B7): a stage, a model and provider, or a budget purpose (with its label).
CostGroup.title: CostGroup

CostSince.description: What was spent from `costs.count_from` (00:00 UTC of that day) to now.
CostSince.title: CostSince

CostSummary.description:
GET /costs (6.B7): the recorded cost of model and embedding calls (`models`) and other paid services (`external`) over
a window of budget weeks, in all and per week.
CostSummary.title: CostSummary

Credit.description: One beat of the story and who did it, as the call (or a fact Whitney attested) names them (first-touch rule 5).

actor.description: Who did it: the client, her AI assistant, our strategist, Whitney, our team

did.description: What they did, in a few words
did.title: Did

Credit.title: Credit

CycleOverview.description: GET /summary (6.F2): what Home shows in one read.
CycleOverview.title: CycleOverview

CycleSchedule.description: GET /schedule: the next run with the schedule in words ("Sunday 04:00 America/Chicago").
CycleSchedule.title: CycleSchedule

EditorialMonitoring.description:
The week's editorial monitoring (6.B13): the accepted share against the bar, which counts once Gate 1 is done (at least
`decided_at_least` cards decided, the rule the low-share alert uses), the skip reasons, the cards whose evidence check
raised a flag, and the cycle the week ran on.
EditorialMonitoring.title: EditorialMonitoring

body.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The rest of the email in finished paragraphs, separated by blank lines: the argument, the story, the principle and the change in thinking
body.title: Body

ending.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The closing paragraph with its ask, and the sign-off
ending.title: Ending

opening.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The greeting and the opening paragraph
opening.title: Opening

preview.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The preview text
preview.title: Preview

subject_options.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. Subject lines to choose from
subject_options.title: Subject Options

body.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The rest of the email in short flowing paragraphs separated by blank lines, with one bold key line; no bullet lists
body.title: Body

ending.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The CTA paragraph and the sign-off
ending.title: Ending

job.description: Direction: a short note to the person who makes the asset; never published. What the email does: it tells the whole story and stands alone
job.title: Job

offer_descriptor.description: Where this asset names an offer: that offer's approved descriptor, word for word from the offer descriptors in the knowledge base; null when it names none
offer_descriptor.title: Offer Descriptor

opening.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The greeting and the opening scene
opening.title: Opening

preview.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The preview text
preview.title: Preview

register.description: written: the email reads like her sent emails, never spoken
register.title: Register

subject_options.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. Two to four subject lines, best first
subject_options.title: Subject Options

EvidencePassage.description: A passage the moment cites, with its role in the scene (`anchor` holds the quote, `context` frames it).
EvidencePassage.title: EvidencePassage

premise_options.description: Three to six premises weighed for the Reels, from different parts of the material, before choosing; empty without the reel channel
premise_options.title: Premise Options

GateContext.description:
Context or an attested fact at either gate (5.B7, R57; interface 2). `author` is whose statement it is when a team
member relays it (R45); the signed-in person when left out.
GateContext.title: GateContext

GateContextItem.description: Context or an attested fact given at a gate (5.B7, R57; interface 2).
GateContextItem.title: GateContextItem

HandoffPiece.description: One format-plan piece (E.B23): a stable key from the plan (`reel_1`, `carousel`, `email`, `caption`, `stories`).
HandoffPiece.title: HandoffPiece

HeldCardDue.description: A card held until a date that has come (3.B11's reminder): due back at Gate 1.
HeldCardDue.title: HeldCardDue

do.description: What the reader might do next, or null: the reader decision is optional
do.title: Do

JobRow.description:
A pipeline job row: the progress contract (plan 1, cross-system integration). Progress is read from these fields
and never inferred from elapsed time.
JobRow.title: JobRow

Ledger.description: The evidence ledger on a card (E.B10): bindings, flags, qualifiers, readiness and the critic's view.
Ledger.title: Ledger

LedgerClaim.description: A statement in the copy and what supports it. The fields v2's claim checks read come first, unchanged.
LedgerClaim.title: LedgerClaim

MomentSummary.description:
A moment as the ledger and search show it. `record` is the neutral scene record (or, for earlier moments, the
proposition); the quote is the exact text of the source when `quote_verified` is true.
MomentSummary.title: MomentSummary

NextCycle.description: When the weekly schedule starts the cycle next (3.B11): `at` and `window` are null while the schedule is off.
NextCycle.title: NextCycle

PackAttest.description:
Attest that a flagged sentence is true (R57): it clears the finding, recorded as attested. On an editorial finding
(Round 2) the statement is why the line is fine as it is: the finding is kept, never a fact.
PackAttest.title: PackAttest

PackClearance.description:
Mark a before-publishing note done (P1 to P5, N1...) or a client quote cleared (Q1...): the client's okay, a quote
cleared, a fact checked. Never a gate; recorded with person, date and reference.
PackClearance.title: PackClearance

PackCost.description: One content pack run's cost from its own call records: what the provider reported for each call it sent.
PackCost.title: PackCost

PackCreate.description: Create or retry the pack for an approved v4 brief (POST /briefs/{id}/pack).
PackCreate.title: PackCreate

PackCreativeChoiceV2.description: Round 2 (finisher v3): the openings or premises weighed for one piece, the one chosen and why.
PackCreativeChoiceV2.title: PackCreativeChoiceV2

PackDecisionV2.description: Ready to publish (bound to the manifest) or back to review.
PackDecisionV2.title: PackDecisionV2

PackEdit.description:
A person's edit of one piece: {path: new value}, paths relative to the piece's content (section 5.6). `reason` (Round 2,
WIA's section 9) is why, in the person's words: it stays with the edit and the weekly learning loop reads it.
PackEdit.title: PackEdit

PackFindingV2.description:
A finding on a piece or the pack. `source` fidelity: the fidelity loop's, stored, cleared by an edit of its sentence
or an attestation (R57); `source` check: a deterministic check, recomputed on every read and edit.
PackFindingV2.title: PackFindingV2

PackFinishAgain.description: Finish the pack again: a new run with no new instruction, every person's line kept (section 4.5).
PackFinishAgain.title: PackFinishAgain

PackGrantIn.description:
One granted item (S1, S2... in the order the pack lists "stronger with permission") or a stated fact (no item), in the
person's own words.
PackGrantIn.title: PackGrantIn

PackLockV2.description:
A line a person wrote, kept word for word by every model step: where (Gate 2 or the pack), who, and whether the
person acted under D12's delegation (R55).
PackLockV2.title: PackLockV2

PackMarkPublished.description: A piece marked published: its date, channel and final text, recorded through capture outside the pack's copy.
PackMarkPublished.title: PackMarkPublished

PackNoteV2.description:
A before-publishing note: carried from Gate 2 with its answer, or added by the pack. A client's permission is a note
for whoever posts the piece, never a gate (`client_permission`).
PackNoteV2.title: PackNoteV2

PackProductionV2.description: GET /packs/{id}/production: the pack run's jobs, costs and why it waits, in words.
PackProductionV2.title: PackProductionV2

PackPublicationV2.description: A piece marked published (date, channel, final text), recorded through capture outside the pack's copy.
PackPublicationV2.title: PackPublicationV2

PackQueuedV2.description: POST /briefs/{id}/pack: the pack run created or retried.
PackQueuedV2.title: PackQueuedV2

PackRecordedTake.description:
The post-recording pass (NP.B14): what Whitney said on a face-to-camera Reel's recorded take. It becomes the Reel's
script word for word, locked as the person's, and the caption and covers are written from it.
PackRecordedTake.title: PackRecordedTake

PackRefinish.description:
Finish again with a permission (NP.B15): the finisher re-runs with the granted items and stated facts as evidence
(attested, R57), keeping every person's line.
PackRefinish.title: PackRefinish

PackRevert.description: Use the brief's line for these paths of one piece.

PackSavedV2.description: The answer to an edit, revert, clearance, attestation, decision or Finish again: the pack version to show now.

PackStarted.description:

PackStarted.title: PackStarted

spoken_opening.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The first spoken line; null for on_screen_text

date_to.description: Open end of the window; an explicit offset is required

recipients.description: Direction: a short note to the person who makes the asset; never published. RECIPIENTS: the proposed list or segment, for WIA to confirm

text.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The slide's finished text

why_now.description: Direction: a short note to the person who makes the asset; never published. Why this piece matters for WIA now

client_contribution.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. What the owner contributed

credits.description: Direction: a short note to the person who makes the asset; never published. Who did what, beat by beat, as the call or an attested fact names them

details.description: Direction: a short note to the person who makes the asset; never published. The one or two concrete details the copy uses; never more than two

scene.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. The one real moment, told as a short anonymised story

timestamps.description: Direction: a short note to the person who makes the asset; never published. Where the moment is in the call, as m:ss or m:ss to m:ss, each with what happens there

wia_move.description: Copy: finished words the audience reads or hears, in WIA's voice, ready to publish. What WIA noticed, asked, decided or did
